claim: Dogs' looking time (dwell time to the two agents) did not differ between congruent and incongruent responses
design: within-subject, 2 levels; unit = dog (39 dogs, 152 trials, 1 trial per condition)
test_used: beta GLMM on proportion dwell time, trial_type removed by LRT (glmmTMB)
test_indicated: same, or paired test on dog means

claim: The number of gaze transitions between the two actresses did not differ between congruent and incongruent responses
design: within-subject, 2 levels; unit = dog (39 dogs, 152 trials)
test_used: Poisson GLMM with log(trial dwell time) offset, trial_type LRT (lme4)
test_indicated: same, or paired test on dog means

claim: Pupils dilated more when watching incongruent than congruent responses (headline claim)
design: within-subject; 41 samples per trial at 100 ms (1000-5000 ms window) nested in trial nested in dog
test_used: GAMM (mgcv::bam, ML, discrete): parametric trial_type + s(time, by=trial_type), random smooths by dog and by trial
test_indicated: GAMM is defensible; the dog-level contrast must be reported alongside it
recomputed_p: not reproducible here: the GAMM did not complete in ~2.4 h of fitting in two R environments (mgcv::bam, 4592 rows, 112 trial-level and 28 dog-level factor smooths)
effect: not computed; the dog-level version of the same contrast is C4/C6

claim: The same pupil contrast at the level of the experimental unit: paired t-test on one mean per dog per trial type (authors' aggregate analysis, n=28)
design: paired; unit = dog; 28 dogs with all 4 valid trials
test_indicated: paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank (both defensible)

claim: The pupil contrast is significant by exact Wilcoxon signed-rank, the test the authors switched to after a Shapiro-Wilk test on the difference scores
test_used: exact Wilcoxon signed-rank, selected after Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.0027 on the differences
test_indicated: a test fixed before inspecting the differences; or report both
effect: same contrast as C4; median paired difference -144.4 units

claim: The pupil finding characterises the N = 39 sample the abstract describes
source: abstract (N = 39) read against the authors' code (pupil analysis run on 28 dogs)
test_used: paired t / Wilcoxon on the 28 dogs with all 4 valid trials
test_indicated: the same test on all dogs with both trial types, or an explicit restriction of the claim
recomputed_p: 0.181 (n=37, same data file); 0.442 (n=38, authors' ALL_DATA file)

claim: Dogs looked longer at the reacting agent than at the communicating agent
recomputed_p: 0.00122 (descriptive means reproduce the authors' values exactly)

claim: The trial type x agent type interaction on dwell time was not significant (and was therefore dropped)
test_used: drop1 LRT on the beta GLMM interaction term
test_indicated: same, or paired test on per-dog difference-of-differences

claim: Neither condition (CA/CG/GA/GG) nor its interaction with agent type was significant
design: within-subject, 4 conditions x 2 agents; unit = dog
test_used: LRT of the full against a condition-free beta GLMM (omnibus, 3 + 3 df)
test_indicated: the omnibus test plus the 1-df design-relevant contrast (approaching vs walking-away response)
recomputed_p: 0.069 (Friedman across the 4 conditions on the per-dog agent preference, n=37); 0.0088 for the 1-df approach-vs-walk-away contrast
effect: agent preference 0.277 vs 0.060 of trial dwell time; difference 0.217, 95% CI [0.058, 0.375] (+2606 ms, 95% CI [+657, +4555])

claim: The expectations are context-specific: the same responses elicited surprise following one gesture but not the other
test_used: no separate test in the deposited code: the pupil model contains trial_type and session only, with no condition or response-type term
test_indicated: trial_type x response-type interaction, or the trial_type contrast within each response type

claim: Eye movements were insensitive to the convention violation while pupil size was sensitive to it (a dissociation between measures)
design: three outcomes measured on the same dogs and the same trials
test_used: significance of one outcome set against non-significance of two others; no test of the difference between measures
test_indicated: a measure x trial_type comparison on standardised outcomes, or an explicit statement that the dissociation was not tested
recomputed_p: not computable as a single test; the three outcomes are on non-commensurable scales
effect: dz = -0.47 (pupil, n=28) vs -0.003 (dwell) and 0.049 (transitions), n=38; the dwell and transition CIs do not exclude an effect of the pupil contrast's standardised size

claim: The expectations are not self-centred, because they were evidenced while dogs observed a third-party interaction between two humans
design: third-party observation design; no contrast against a dog-directed condition
test_indicated: a dog-directed comparison condition would be required to test it
